Q: Web NFC API request denied error on Android WebView A:

Although support for the Web NFC API was listed for Android WebView starting from version 89:

  • https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_NFC_API#browser_compatibility

I found a source that stated the following:

Web NFC is not supported in Android Webview. It's mainly due to the fact that Chrome Web NFC shows a prompt in Chrome and prompts are not implemented in Android WebView.

https://github.com/w3c/web-nfc/issues/650

And this appears consistent with my own findings.

When overriding WebChromeClient#onPermissionRequest, there does not appear to be any requests for NFC, so I don't believe it is currently possible to use the Web NFC API on Android WebView.

Q: Sort a Map<Key, Value> by values A:

In TreeMap, keys are sorted in natural order. For example, if you sorting numbers, (notice the ordering of 4)

{0=0, 10=10, 20=20, 30=30, 4=4, 50=50, 60=60, 70=70}

To fix this, in Java 8, first check string length and then compare.

Map<String, String> sortedMap =
    new TreeMap<>Comparator.comparingInt(String::length)
                           .thenComparing(Function.identity()));

{0=0, 4=4, 10=10, 20=20, 30=30, 50=50, 60=60, 70=70}

Q: Android 15 navigation bar icons appear dark even on a dark background A:

For Android 15, API 35, the system altered the handling of icon contrast in the navigation bar. The flag used in the application’s XML file, as shown below, is not always honored if the system feels it has to force contrast, particularly under the following conditions:

* The application has an edge-to-edge screen.

* The color of the navigation bar is fully transparent or nearly black.

* Gesture navigation is enabled.

In all of these scenarios, the system forces dark icons, even if you try to override this with the following flag: android:windowLightNavigationBar.

maybe disabling contrast could fix the problem

getWindow().setNavigationBarContrastEnforced(false);

https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/layout/edge-to-edge
